title: Fu Manchu
paragraphs: Serialized radio adaptations of Sax Rohmer's Fu Manchu stories, following the struggle of Nayland Smith and Dr. Petrie against the schemes of the brilliant and dangerous criminal mastermind.
It adapts Sax Rohmer novels in continuing 15-minute chapters.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: 1939 Radio Attractions serial slice (May 8, 1939 to November 4, 1939).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Hanley Stafford (performer), [[person|gale-gordon|Gale Gordon]] (performer and announcer), [[person|gerald-mohr|Gerald Mohr]] (announcer and performer), Lou Marcelle (performer), Paula Winslowe (performer), [[person|edmond-obrien|Edmond O’Brien]] (performer), and [[person|howard-mcnear|Howard McNear]] (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8b1104e3b833338e|Radio Attractions]].

The stories often return to international and colonial settings, secret societies and hidden networks, murder and attempted murder, science used as a threat or weapon, abduction and captivity, and poisons and exotic toxins.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Transcription syndication through Radio Attractions, Sax Rohmer novel-to-radio serial adaptation, Fu Manchu and Yellow Peril popular imagery, and Interwar serial cliffhanger culture.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|escape|Escape]], [[show|the-railroad-hour|The Railroad Hour]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], and [[show|broadway-is-my-beat|Broadway Is My Beat]].
plain_text:
Serialized radio adaptations of Sax Rohmer's Fu Manchu stories, following the struggle of Nayland Smith and Dr. Petrie against the schemes of the brilliant and dangerous criminal mastermind.

It adapts Sax Rohmer novels in continuing 15-minute chapters.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: 1939 Radio Attractions serial slice (May 8, 1939 to November 4, 1939).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Hanley Stafford (performer), Gale Gordon (performer and announcer), Gerald Mohr (announcer and performer), Lou Marcelle (performer), Paula Winslowe (performer), Edmond O’Brien (performer), and Howard McNear (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to Radio Attractions.

The stories often return to international and colonial settings, secret societies and hidden networks, murder and attempted murder, science used as a threat or weapon, abduction and captivity, and poisons and exotic toxins.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Transcription syndication through Radio Attractions, Sax Rohmer novel-to-radio serial adaptation, Fu Manchu and Yellow Peril popular imagery, and Interwar serial cliffhanger culture.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include Lux Radio Theatre, Escape, The Railroad Hour, Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar, and Broadway Is My Beat.
